beats: Hook: in Java you drop a temporary and the garbage collector frees it (her comparison, Q25-08 38:30-39:14; Q24-13 19:55-20:31): line_qc_scratch_robot_sweep. Do the same with a scratch qubit, measure it and reuse it, and you can destroy the answer you meant to keep. Why? Same cast as QC07-01: the keeper and the rookie (cast drawing line_qc_revers_fresh_card); the little robot comes back as the helper that cleans up for you.

AND of three bits with two Toffolis and a scratch qubit (35:36-38:30): the scratch holds a AND b, the output holds abc; code letters the circuit; the kept cards of line_qc_revers_card_haul (QC07-01) are the garbage.

Why not just measure it? (39:14-46:30; Q24-13 20:45-23:28) The scratch is entangled with the answer, as in |000> + |110>, so reading it picks one branch and the superposition you were computing on is gone: line_qc_scratch_tied_cards (caption: the thread pictures the correlation; it is not a force); reuse line_dice_hand for the random branch. Clip 45:19-46:06.

Uncompute instead: run the same Toffoli again (it is its own inverse) and the scratch returns to 0, unentangled and free (46:30-51:42; clip 47:58-48:25, "measurement is not the right thing"); reuse line_qc_build_two_keys (turn the same two keys back) and line_qc_undo_twist_cube.

The general pattern (51:44-54:22; Q24-13 30:04-31:07; Bennett 1973: check in FACTS.md): compute, copy the result out, run the computation backwards: put up the scaffold, hang the lantern, take the scaffold down from the top (line_qc_scratch_scaffold_up, then line_qc_scratch_scaffold_down); reuse line_qc_build_pebble_trail (QC05-06) for walking the steps back. Tape Q25-08 s56 and Q24-13.notes p4.

The trade: undoing costs extra gates (time) and gives the qubits back (49:45-50:12; Q24-13 25:45-26:11, her answer only: the student question 24:33-26:21 is never used): the same poles go up on the next house (line_qc_scratch_poles_next); reuse line_balance.

Programmers will not do this by hand; compilers should, as runtimes do garbage collection (clip Q24-13 31:16-31:40; Q24-05 61:31-62:24 for uncomputation inside multi-controlled gates): the robot takes the scaffold down overnight, top first, while the two sleep (line_qc_scratch_night_robot).
Better uncomputation strategies are an open research problem (54:30-55:32): reuse line_qc_build_jigsaw or line_paper.
Cover (line_qc_cover_07_02; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the rookie dangles a scratch card over the bin; a thread is dragging the answer card off the desk; the keeper lunges.
